Duration arithmetic¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Duration Duration::operator+(const Duration& other) const;
Duration Duration::operator-(const Duration& other) const;
Duration Duration::operator-() const;
Duration& Duration::operator+=(const Duration& other);
Duration& Duration::operator-=(const Duration& other);

Duration Duration::mul(std::int64_t k) const;
Duration Duration::operator*(std::int64_t k) const;
Duration Duration::div(std::int64_t k) const;
Duration Duration::operator/(std::int64_t k) const;
Duration Duration::floordiv(std::int64_t k) const;
Duration Duration::mod(std::int64_t k) const;

What It Does¶

Duration + Duration and Duration - Duration combine two elapsed-time values elementwise, broadcasting via the same SeriesIterator machinery every other N-D op in Pluss uses. Unary -Duration negates (flips “forward in time” to “backward in time” and back). +=/-= are ordinary compound-assignment sugar around the two binary operators.

mul/div/floordiv/mod scale a Duration by a plain integer count k — not by another Duration — since “a duration times a duration” isn’t a meaningful elapsed-time value (compare: Series * Series is fine because both sides are unitless numbers; Duration * Duration would need to be an elapsed-time-squared, which nothing here represents).

Parameters¶

other (const Duration&)

The other duration, for the binary operators. Broadcasts against self under ordinary N-D rules.

k (std::int64_t)

A plain integer scale/divisor/modulus. mod’s k is a raw nanosecond count (not “a number of days” or similar), so computing “remainder after dividing by 3 days” means passing 3 * 86'400 * 1'000'000'000LL, not 3 — see Example 3.

Returns¶

Duration A new duration holding the elementwise result. operator+=/operator-= instead mutate self and return Duration&.

Examples¶

Example 1. Add and subtract two durations built from different units.

auto ninety_min = pluss::duration::minutes(90);
auto one_hour = pluss::duration::hours(1);
auto one_day = pluss::duration::days(1);
std::cout << "sum=" << pluss::print_series((ninety_min + one_hour).total_hours()) << "\n";
std::cout << "diff=" << pluss::print_series((one_day - one_hour).total_hours());

Output¶

sum=Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=2.5000
diff=Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=23.0000

90 min + 1 h = 2.5 h; 1 day - 1 h = 23 h.

Example 2. Unary negation and scalar mul/div.

auto one_hour = pluss::duration::hours(1);
auto one_day = pluss::duration::days(1);
std::cout << "neg=" << pluss::print_series((-one_hour).total_hours()) << "\n";
std::cout << "times3=" << pluss::print_series((one_hour * 3).total_hours()) << "\n";
std::cout << "div4=" << pluss::print_series((one_day / 4).total_hours());

Output¶

neg=Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=-1.0000
times3=Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=3.0000
div4=Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=6.0000

-1 h; 1 h * 3 = 3 h; 1 day / 4 = 6 h.

Example 3. mod against a raw nanosecond divisor, over a Duration array.

auto ranged = pluss::duration::range(
    pluss::duration::days(0), pluss::duration::days(10), pluss::duration::days(2));
constexpr std::int64_t kThreeDaysNanos = 3LL * 86'400 * 1'000'000'000LL;
std::cout << pluss::print_series(ranged.mod(kThreeDaysNanos).total_days());

Output¶

Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 2.0000, 1.0000, 0.0000, 2.0000, 1.0000]

[0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10] days each mod 3 days, elementwise: 0, 2, 1, 0, 2, 1. k had to be 3 * 86'400 * 1'000'000'000 (three days’ worth of nanoseconds), not the bare integer 3 — passing 3 would compute “days mod 3 nanoseconds,” not “days mod 3 days.”

Example 4. +=/-= mutate self in place and are verified identical to the binary operators they wrap.

auto compound_add = one_hour;
compound_add += ninety_min;
std::cout << "sum=" << pluss::print_series(compound_add.total_hours()) << "\n";
std::cout << "matches_binary=" << pluss::print_series(compound_add.eq(one_hour + ninety_min));

Output¶

sum=Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=2.5000
matches_binary=Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=true

Notes¶

  • mul/div/floordiv/mod all take a plain std::int64_t, not a Duration — there is no “divide one duration by another” operation on this surface (that would produce a unitless ratio, not a Duration, and isn’t implemented here).

  • mod’s divisor is always raw nanoseconds, regardless of what unit you’re conceptually thinking in — convert explicitly, as in Example 3.

  • Duration also combines with Timeline: Timeline + Duration and Timeline - Duration both exist, documented on Timeline::add_duration.
